about: Auditory streaming: when successive tones hold together as one line, when they split into streams (a compound melody's voices), and when they merge into one tone. Read by the streaming judgement (public/shared/performers/streams.js) and the figures it judges (figure-space.js).

fission-boundary.conditions: two pure tones alternating (ABAB), 40 ms each, B at 1 kHz, 35 dB SL, by headphones; two observers, each told to hear the B tones alone; tone repetition times T of 0.1 to 0.4 s
fission-boundary.note: the least interval at which a listener attending to one string can hear the tones apart, two streams: below it they always hold together. Practically independent of T in that range; wider at shorter T (peripheral effects make selecting one string impossible) and at longer T (the string's tones too far apart in time)

temporal-coherence-boundary.where: section 5.5, Fig. 5.11 (its circled means, read to about a semitone and 10 ms); the point at the origin his extrapolation
temporal-coherence-boundary.conditions: random sequences of pure tones, each interval drawn about a mean, tone durations D of 40 to 400 ms, none overlapping, by headphones; observers trying to hear all the tones as one line
temporal-coherence-boundary.note: the interval past which a tone can no longer be heard with its neighbours as one line, against the gap from the end of the tone before it to the start of the tone after it (2T - D): one curve for every tone duration, so a legato or overlapping tone's boundary is the narrower; at a gap of none, none (the tones before and after sound with it). Probably so for partly overlapping tones too, which his equipment could not make. Between this and the fission boundary a tone is heard either way, as the listener attends

trill-threshold.where: as van Noorden 1975 reports it, sections 1.3 and 2.5
trill-threshold.conditions: two pure tones alternating ten times a second (T = 0.1 s), each filling the time to the next (a gap of 0.1 s)
trill-threshold.note: the interval past which a trill is heard as two tones, two streams. At its gap, where Fig. 5.11's temporal coherence boundary stands at 2.6 semitones; van Noorden found it the mean of his two boundaries at the same T with tones of 40 ms (a gap of 0.16 s)

fusion-repetition-time.conditions: pure-tone sequences of small intervals (a semitone), random or ascending
fusion-repetition-time.note: below about this tone repetition time a sequence of small intervals merges into one tone, modulated in frequency and amplitude: one line, its tones no longer each heard. So, he expects, the fastest runs (Bach's cello suites: 81 ms) and trills
